title: ThruLines #008
phrase: Instead of something I want, can it be something I don't want?

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which US city is nicknamed the City of Brotherly Love?
questions.connectionNote: The setting — the whole story haunts Philadelphia.

questions.subject: Slang
questions.prompt: What's it called when someone abruptly stops answering your texts?
questions.connectionNote: Ghosting — the pun writes itself, and it's also literally what's happening to one character all movie.

questions.subject: Movies
questions.prompt: Which action film may or may not be a Christmas movie, depending on who you ask?
questions.connectionNote: Bruce Willis — John McClane before he was Malcolm Crowe.

questions.subject: Show Business
questions.prompt: Macaulay Culkin, Millie Bobby Brown and Shirley Temple are all famous examples of what?
questions.connectionNote: Haley Joel Osment earned an Oscar nomination at eleven — one of the great child-actor performances.

questions.subject: World Cinema
questions.prompt: Which Australian movie is famously wall-to-wall ABBA songs?
questions.connectionNote: Toni Collette's breakout — five years before she played the mother here.

reveal.summary: The Sixth Sense. Philadelphia is the setting, ghosting is the pun, Die Hard is Bruce Willis, the child actors point to Haley Joel Osment, and Muriel's Wedding is Toni Collette before the minivan scene. The line is the film's quiet bargaining — asking for the absence of something, which is the whole movie in one sentence.
reveal.ohMoment: Every answer was circling one table in an Italian restaurant — where a wife has dinner alone on her anniversary.

editorial.notes: Phrase switched to the author's shorter alternate (48 letters) to fit the mobile board budget. VERBATIM CHECK still needed against the script before wide release.
